data.gender_notes: Uziel is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Uziel means 'God of help' or 'Strength of God'. It is derived from the Hebrew roots 'ez' meaning help and 'el' meaning God. The name Uziel carries the meaning “God of help” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Uziel usually hope their child will grow to embody god of help and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of divine intervention and strength.
data.etymology: Uziel belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of help.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Uziel total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_hebrew.name: עוּזִיאֵל
in_hebrew.meaning: אב בנות, שמחת נפש, קדוש ונאמן.
in_hebrew.long_meaning: עוּזִיאֵל הוא שם עברי, נראה כמנוון עברית, המופיע במקרא. השם מורכב משני מילים: עוז (כוח, עז) ואיאל (אל, אלוהים). עוז ואיאל יחדיו - 'אל שהוא עז' - ראשי תיבות למשפחת הכוהנים מן השבט שבט לוי. בעברית הקדומה, 'עוּזִיאֵל' (עוּז = 'עז' וִאֵל = 'אל') נכתב 'עוּזִאֵל' (עוז + אל). המקרא מזכיר 16 אישים עם השם 'עוּזִאֵל' - 8 בן-טוב, 8 בן-סירא, 3 בן-אלעזר, 3 בן-אלעזר (כל השבט).

in_greek.name: Οὐζέλ
in_greek.long_meaning: Ὁ ὄνομα Οὐζέλ, ἐπὶ τοῦ ἐνόμου τοῦ Ἰουδαϊσμοῦ. Ἀναφέρεται σὲ 16 ἀνθρώπους σὲ τὴν Βίβλο, πᾶσαν ἀπὸ τὸ Ἰσραήλ. Ἀπὸ τὸ ἑβραϊκό ῾עוּזִיאֵל, ῾עוז + ῾אל, τὸ ῾אל, τὸ θεόν. Σὲ τὴν Βίβλο, ὁ Οὐζέλ, εἶναι ὁ ἀνδρικός.

in_latin.name: Uziel
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Uziel, secundum legem Judaeorum. In Biblia, sunt 16 homines, omnes ex Israel. Ex hebraico Usiel, Us + El, El, Deum. In Biblia, Uziel, est virilis.

in_english.name: Uziel
in_english.meaning: strength of God, a masculine name with a strong biblical background.
in_english.long_meaning: Uziel is a Hebrew name, formed by 'Us' (strength) and 'El' (God). The name appears in the Bible, where 16 individuals with this name are mentioned. In the Hebrew Bible, the name Uziel is associated with the tribe of Levi. Uziel is a name with a strong biblical background and a masculine connotation. It symbolizes strength and power, reflecting the characteristics of its namesake. Uziel is a rare and unique name, but its meaning and history make it an attractive choice for parents seeking a name with depth and significance.

data.cultural_impact: The name Uziel has been used in various cultures and belief systems beyond Christianity. In Jewish tradition, Uziel is considered one of the prophets. In Islam, Uzayr is a prophet described in various hadiths, and his name is believed to be derived from Uziel. Uziel is also mentioned in the Muslim Qisas al-Anbiya (Stories of the Prophets), a collection of stories about prophets in Muslim literature.
data.spiritual_significance: Uziel is a powerful name that symbolizes the belief in God's help and strength. It conveys the message that no matter what challenges one may face, God is always there to provide support and guidance. For many Christians, the name Uziel may serve as a reminder to turn to God for strength and help in times of need. It may also be seen as a name that embodies the qualities of God, such as compassion, love, and power. Ultimately, Uziel is a name that inspires faith and hope in the presence and power of God.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Uziel is a Hebrew name meaning "God of help" or "strength of God." It is a name given to those who believe in the divine assistance and protection of God in times of need.

biblical_reference.note: Uziel is a Levite and the father of Zerahiah in the Bible.

historical_references.reference: Uziel is mentioned in the Old Testament as the name of a priestly descendants of Aaron, the brother of Moses. This lineage is recorded in the Book of Numbers, chapter 3:10.
Uziel is also mentioned in the New Testament as the name of a prophet who is said to have foretold the coming of the Messiah. This prophecy is recorded in the Book of Matthew, chapter 1:21.
